text: Morning. Have you got any {requestedPotion}? I've left my cart where the geese can get at it.
A small bottle of {requestedPotion}, please. My sister wrote it down after I came home with lamp oil last time.
Could I get some {requestedPotion}? I promised I'd be back before the bread came out.
One {requestedPotion}, if you please. Wrap it in paper. The eggs in my basket have had a rough enough morning.
Do you sell {requestedPotion} by the bottle? I've only ever bought it by the spoonful.
That's the one. Thank you kindly.
Much obliged. Now to see what the geese have left me.
Thanks. I'll put it somewhere safer than the egg basket.
Perfect. I might make it home while the bread's still warm.
Good, I can read that label. Last shop wrote theirs in silver ink the size of fleas.
I'd better leave that here. I was sent for {requestedPotion}.
That says {brewedPotion}. I can read that much, at least.
Could you check the shelf again? I need {requestedPotion} before I head home.
If I bring that back, my sister will make me walk here again.
I'm sure it's good for something. What I need today is {requestedPotion}.
I need {requestedPotion}. My apprentice borrowed the last bottle and returned it remarkably clean.
A vial of {requestedPotion}, please. I'd brew it myself, but my cauldron has taken to answering back.
Have you any {requestedPotion}? I've a lecture in an hour and my demonstration is still climbing the curtains.
One bottle of {requestedPotion}. Write the name on the glass, if you would. I've had a disagreement with a loose label.
Could you spare a dose of {requestedPotion}? My notes say I have three. My cupboard has lodged an objection.
Precisely what I needed. I'll keep this one on the shelf my apprentice can't reach.
Excellent. I can postpone a very tedious afternoon of brewing.
Thank you. I was beginning to consider canceling the practical demonstration.
Good seal. I once lost a week's work to a cork I'd cut myself.
Much appreciated. I'll make a note to buy the next bottle before I need it.
That's {brewedPotion}. I recognize the sediment. I asked for {requestedPotion}.
An interesting brew. I can think of three uses for it, and none concerns my errand.
My apprentice makes that mistake too. Put it aside and look for {requestedPotion}.
I would taste it to settle the matter, but that's how I lost my eyebrows the first time.
Let's check the labels before either of us starts defending a hypothesis.
Got {requestedPotion}? Small bottle. Big bottles bang against my knees in the tunnels.
One {requestedPotion}. I brought back last week's bottle. See? Even washed the outside.
I need {requestedPotion}. Put the cork in tight. My bag's mostly holes.
A bottle of {requestedPotion}, please. Can you write the name on it big enough to read by one candle?
You sell {requestedPotion}? Good. The fellow under the bridge offered me soup in a fancy bottle.
Good cork. Doesn't budge. I'll remember this shop.
That fits my pocket. You'd be surprised how many shops get that wrong.
Thanks. I'll bring the bottle back if I don't find a better use for it.
That's it. And I can read the whole label without turning the bottle. Nice.
Much better than bridge soup. Keep a bottle handy next time I'm through.
Wrong bottle. Good cork, though. Where's my {requestedPotion}?
If I wanted a mystery bottle, I'd pick one out of the river for free.
That says {brewedPotion}. I sounded the whole thing out. Still wrong.
I could probably trade this, but then I'd have to come back for {requestedPotion}.
Hang on. Set that down before you wrap it. I'm not walking home with the wrong thing again.
Is the shop still open? I came for {requestedPotion}. I lose track of time after sunset.
A vial of {requestedPotion}, please. Leave it on the counter. I still have trouble taking things from people's hands.
Could I buy {requestedPotion}? I brought a coin from the year the old bridge opened. I hope it still spends.
Do you carry {requestedPotion}? There was an apothecary on this corner when the well was still here.
One {requestedPotion}, if you please. I waited outside for the bell to ring before I remembered it had been taken down.
Thank you. I think I remember how to carry a bottle without dropping it.
Much obliged. I had forgotten how pleasant it is to be expected at a counter.
You found it. I'll leave the coin where you can see it.
Thank you for keeping a light in the window. It makes this street easier to find.
That's the bottle. I'll take the long way home. The old steps are still there.
I may have spoken too softly. I asked for {requestedPotion}.
Leave that on the counter a moment. I think it belongs to someone else.
I remember ordering {requestedPotion}. My memory's patchy, but that was just now.
The bottle is familiar. The label says {brewedPotion}. Would you look again?
I have made enough trips down this street to know when I need {requestedPotion}.
One vial of {requestedPotion}. Wrap it well. The road back to the lower hall will shake the nails out of a cart.
Have you got {requestedPotion}? I'm crossing the pass with my brothers, and we leave when the smith shuts his doors.
A bottle of {requestedPotion}, please. I've room for it between my chisels if the glass is thick enough.
I'll take {requestedPotion}. Put my name on it. Three of us share a bench, and two of us can't keep our hands to ourselves.
Could you fill an order for {requestedPotion}? The last shop sent me up three flights of stairs to tell me they were out.
Well sealed. I'd trust that bottle in the bottom of my tool chest.
Good work. I'll tell the crew where I got it.
That's what I ordered. I'll be back when the road opens again.
My thanks. I can make the first lift down if I leave now.
I appreciate the care. Whoever packed my last bottle could learn a thing from you.
Check the order. I asked for {requestedPotion}, and I've a crew waiting.
Save the wrapping. I can't take {brewedPotion} back to the hall.
The bottle's sound. The contents are wrong.
Set it by the other order. I'll wait here while you find the {requestedPotion}.
I've carried the wrong parcel over a mountain once. I learned to read the label at the counter.
A vial of {requestedPotion}, please. I'm taking the forest road before the rain reaches the ford.
Do you have {requestedPotion}? I used to find this shop by the old pear tree. The tree is gone, and your sign could stand to be larger.
One bottle of {requestedPotion}, if you have it. I promised to meet my companion where the west road forks.
I've come for {requestedPotion}. Could you wrap it in cloth? The glass will knock against my flute all the way home.
May I have some {requestedPotion}? I'd rather buy it here than cross the river again after dark.
Thank you. I should reach the ford before the water rises.
Much appreciated. I'll remember the door next time.
That's what I came for. You've saved me a walk to the far side of the river.
Thank you for the cloth. The last shopkeeper packed my bottle in dried leaves. I heard it for three miles.
My thanks. If the pear tree ever grows back, your shop will be very easy to find.
Would you look at the label with me? I asked for {requestedPotion}.
I know that scent. Someone else may be waiting for this bottle.
That's {brewedPotion}. I've carried it before. What I need today is {requestedPotion}.
Set it aside for its owner. I have time for you to check the order.
I'd rather sort this out here than discover it halfway across the ford.
